purpose: Prove the constitution's terminal product proposition through an environment-attributed finite repeated-natural-task cohort: sustained goal-level delivery, lower user orchestration burden than same-starting-environment source-bound ad-hoc baselines, real demand-driven capability and carrier lifecycles, and live cross-host open reference delivery. v0.2 remains an immutable bounded calibration milestone and v1.0 remains an immutable stopped zero-outcome attempt; neither can satisfy this program by inheritance.

increments.observedProblem: The current verifier can now recognize and irreversibly pin the reviewed v1.1 profile and cohort-protocol binding, but the current human-authorization validator identity and registry remain unavailable and every existing private-source validator is bound to stopped v1.0 generations. A v1.1 freeze would therefore fail closed even after an exact independent human authorization, while reusing the v1.0 private resource would violate the current authority and environment boundary.
increments.hypothesis: A dedicated inactive v1.1 first-freeze authorization validator contract, with a distinct current-user protected-resource namespace, versioned source commitments, exact retention and revocation semantics, and null execution-specific anchors until a later authorized freeze, can make the current activation route verifiable without reading or creating private evidence, activating a cohort, or weakening the freeze chronology.
increments.falsifier: Stop and remove the mechanism if it reuses a v1.0 credential, source event, commitment or activation identity; accepts an authorization before an exact committed freeze; reads or creates a private resource while the v1.1 binding is unfrozen; embeds a private locator or value in public state; permits a missing, ambiguous, changed, expired or post-revocation source to pass; performs cohort activation; adds an acceptance threshold; or cannot remain fail-closed with all execution-specific anchors unset.
increments.stopCondition: Stop after one exact v1.1-only authorization validator seam and protected-resource lifecycle contract are code-owned, unit tests prove v1.0 reuse, unset anchors, malformed private evidence, source drift, expiry and revocation fail closed, the live unfrozen program performs no private read and remains valid with O1-O5 at 0/5, canonical and product tests pass, no private resource or consumer is created or changed, all task-created residue is removed, and this outcome-neutral increment exits the current graph.

deliverables: one inactive v1.1-only first-freeze source-authorization validator contract
one fail-closed current-user protected-resource lifecycle seam with unset execution anchors
focused regression coverage proving no v1.0 reuse, no unfrozen private read and no cohort activation
